newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-Blowers a double nominee for rugby awards.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-Blowers a double nominee for rugby awards.

text.p: WELLINGTON, Oct 31 - Outstanding young All Blacks flanker Andrew Blowers has been nominated in two categories for next month's New Zealand rugby awards.

Blowers, who made a huge impression as a mid-week player and test reserve during New Zealand's tour of South Africa in August, is in line for the age grade award as well as the new Super 12 award, NZPA reported on Thursday.

The Auckland open-side flanker is up against Otago hooker Anton Oliver and North Harbour halfback Mark Robinson in the age grade category and faces competition from Blues teammate Joeli Vidiri and Wellington Hurricanes prop Mark Allen in the Super
All Blacks captain Sean Fitzpatrick is one of three players in line to win the game's most coveted individual award, the Kelvin Tremain Memorial Award.

Fitzpatrick, who steered the All Blacks to nine wins out of 10 tests this year, star flanker Michael Jones and outstanding halfback Justin Marshall are the three candidates to win the trophy named in memory of the great All Blacks flanker of the 1960s.
Marshall, Auckland midfield back Eroni Clarke and surprise nominee Counties-Manukau second five-eighth Tony Marsh are the three finalists for the first division player of the year title.
All Blacks coach John Hart, Auckland coach Graham Henry and Mac McCallion, coach of Counties-Manukau, are the three finalists for the coach of the year award.

In other categories, Vanessa Cootes (Waikato), Helen Littlewood (Otago) and Annaleah Rush (Otago) are nominated for women's player of the year while Colin Hawke (South Canterbury), Paddy O'Brien (Southland) and Glenn Wahlstrom (Auckland) are in line to be named top referee.

Nelson's Chris England, Southland's Norm Hewitt and Northland's Glen Taylor are finalists in the division two player award and Rob Penney (Marlborough), Thomas Stewart (Buller) and Peter Thomas (Wanganui) are up for the division three award.
Winners of the Tom French Cup (outstanding Maori player) and the Sevens award will be named at the awards dinner in Auckland on November 7.
